recipes.name: PHILLY Bavarian Apple Torte
ingredients_raw: 1 (250 g) package PHILADELPHIA Brick Cream Cheese, softened
4 Granny Smith or Golden Delicious apples, peeled, sliced

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).

Beat 1/3 cup sugar and butter together in a small bowl with an electric mixer on medium speed until light and fluffy. Add flour; mix well. Spread crust on the bottom and 1 inch up the sides of a 9-inch springform pan.

Beat cream cheese and 1/3 cup sugar in same bowl with an electric mixer on medium speed until well blended. Add egg and vanilla extract; mix well. Spread evenly over crust. Combine remaining 1/3 cup sugar and cinnamon. Toss with apples in a large bowl. Spoon over cream cheese layer; sprinkle with almonds.

Bake in the preheated oven for 10 minutes. Reduce heat to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C); continue to bake until center is set, about 25 minutes. Cool on a wire rack. Loosen torte from rim of the pan. Cover and refrigerate 3 hours before serving. Store any leftovers in the refrigerator.

raw_recipe.headline: PHILLY Bavarian Apple Torte
raw_recipe.description: This PHILLY Bavarian apple torte recipe is easy to prepare and is a rich, delicious dessert topped with almonds and apples tossed with cinnamon-sugar.

review.reviewBody: I Made this recipe for a party and it went fast. I did not have the required pan so I used my regular pie pan and it turned out great. I layered the apples like the picture and sprinkled almonds and it looked very beautiful. Some skins I left on for looks.

Wonderful dessert! I'm sure the recipe is great as is, but still made following changes: Added ground flax seed and ground almond to the crust, and added ricotta cheese to the filling. I only used 3 granny smith apples as I cut them very thinly. I baked at lower temperature for longer time to get the apples more tender. Still not fully cooked, but good enough. Great presentation for sure! Oh and I baked in 8" pan to get the sides go up a little bit more. Both the filling and crust are delicious!

This is my go to for a quick come together desert, as I generally have all the ingredients at home (except apples). A little tweak that I added for even more flavor is lemon zest and fresh juice added to the apples, and 2-3 tablespoons of fresh lemon juice to the cream cheese mixture. You could use orange zest and juice if you prefer. Play around with your apples for a beautiful design to impress! I also drizzled some of the Apple liquid on top of the Apples after they are laid out. Don’t forget to put a sheet pan under to catch potential drips. This is sure to be a favorite of yours and your guests!

I made mine in a 9" springform pan and I doubled the recipe for the crust and the filling. I didn't use all the crust batter but just enough to make a thin layer on the bottom and an inch + on the sides. I did use all the filling. I cooked it for about 50 minutes and it came out perfect. I have also made this topped with cherry pie filling being careful to not use much of the syrupy part, but just mostly the cherries. To top my torte with these enough cherries took about 1 1/2 - 21 oz cans. It's a very impressive dessert with little effort.

We absolutely loved this recipe! Loved it so much that we finished off the entire thing in one sitting!!

It was extremely easy to cook up. I loved the crust, I’m thinking of doubling it next time so I could get more. 
The flavors were just right. I didn’t change a thing. I only added nutmeg to the apples. I also left it in the oven for 20 mins then turned on the broiler for 5 mins, Just to brown the apples a bit and make them crunchy.
A definite keeper.

I MADE THIS TWO TIMES OVER 3 DAYS. Lol

Three times in a week.......wow!!

Beautiful and delicious! Making for thanksgiving in addition to the required pumpkin pie. Have made this before to rave reviews. Tripled the cheesecake mixture as I used a10” springform pan. No almonds as not all like them.

Awesome dessert - I received lots of praise for this one. The only thing I did a little differently was that I didn't have the almonds, and it looked like it needed something to garnish the top, so I drizzled caramel ice cream topping on top. When I make it for Thanksgiving, I'm going to try walnuts (which I prefer over almonds) AND the caramel.

By the way, I saw a comment about having difficulty spreading the pastry in the bottom, so here's a tip: Lay a piece of wax paper on top then use your hands or a spatula to spread it out evenly on the pan.

I originally made this recipe many times years ago from a leaflet of Philadelphia Cream Cheese recipes and was glad to find it years later here on All Recipes. It's very easy and one of the best cheesecake recipes ever--everyone loves the combination of flavors. I usually make one and a half times the recipe and use a 9 or 10 inch springform pan because I like the cream cheese filling and crust to come up a little higher on the sides--the amount of apples can remain the same as the original--but finely chop them, don't slice them. You will probably need to bake it a 10-15 minutes longer to make sure the center is set. I had several people tell me this was the best dessert they'd ever had at the last potluck I took it to.

I followed the instructions just as written, with one tiny addition! I chopped up about 1/4 cup of almonds very fine and added that to the crust. I sliced my apples very thin, as some other reviewers had suggested, but I did need to cook it about 10 minutes longer than the recipe called for to see that the middle was set. Could be a difference in oven temp, but something to watch for. This was sooooo delish and looked beautiful! Everyone loved it. I'll absolutely make it again!

Double the cheesecake filling use almond extract instead of or with the vanilla. Absolutely must use granny smiths or another firm cooking apple. Slice as evenly as possible less than 1/4in.I've made this lots of times

Made it last night. Followed recipe very closely, but to switch it up a bit with the spice, I reduced the cinnamon and used some freshly grated nutmeg, freshly ground cardamom, and powdered ginger in addition. I also baked in 8 inch pan, by suggestion of another review to make a deeper torte. We couldn't wait the 3 hours to chill. Once it cooled from the oven, we cut and dug in. Yum!
I made this for work parties for several years. One year my boss asked me to make (he'd pay) him one so that he could take it with him on the plane to Florida for Thanksgiving!

I make this ALL THE TIME. This is my go-to for potluck type events. But I make 2 changes from what is listed here. I do not use almonds at all. And I add 1 tablespoon of Disarrono to the filling when I add the vanilla.Admittedly, I have also made this with a variety of different apples as well. I find that anything with a medium texture is best, nothing mushy and nothing too hard. I would also recommend a moderately sweet to tart apple, not a really sweet kind for this.

Used a springform pan as suggested, but some of the butter melted out of the crust onto the bottom of the oven & started smoking.Also, when the cake was done, the apples were still a little uncooked.Has this happened to anyone else?
not going to bother, found crust pain to make & made mess in oven. only needed 3 apples (make sure to spray/grease pan)
Make exactly as directed. Had to make 2 layers of apples but it was good. In fact, would prefer just a touch more apples. Guests ended up preferring the German Apple Cake II over this one though.
Beautiful, easy, delicious and impressive!
made with gluten free flour. doubled cinnamon
I don’t like cheesecake so I figured my family would like this and I would not, but it really is not a cheesecake. This was delicious, and so simple to make.
Very tasty! I’ve never done a crust like this so I was a little curious how it would turn out but it all turned out great!
